results.why: Both candidates score whether the setup (data sources, models/scale, protocol, comparison setting, outcomes) is reported completely enough to reconstruct the experiment, which is exactly the target's experiment-and-model reporting transparency in ML vocabulary.
No candidate scores funding, conflict-of-interest, sponsor-role, or acknowledgment disclosure at all.

K28 explicitly scores methods/analysis detail plus usable artifacts sufficient to audit or reconstruct the contribution, and K18 the same for the experiment, which is the target's methods-and-code transparency/reproducibility-readiness property.
The structural candidates (K03, K07, K35) judge whether one idea organizes the text, and K03 explicitly says to judge structure not length, so none scores conciseness, length, or venue-format fit.
No candidate scores software functionality, architecture, code quality, maintainability, or usability as a research artifact.

Description of groups/arms, units, allocation and timing is at most a sub-part of the much broader operational-specificity candidates (K18/K28), and no candidate targets design description on its own.

Same property in ML register: whether procedural detail is specific enough to permit independent replication, with the target's who/when/dosage vocabulary corresponding to the candidates' data/protocol/model/comparison details.
Nothing in the candidate set scores venue aims-and-scope fit or baseline submission eligibility.

The target is procedural and analytical detail sufficient for independent replication, which is precisely what K18 and K28 score (protocol, comparison procedure, measurable outcomes, artifacts) in ML wording.

K53 is the nearest neighbour but scores how informative the resource description is and explicitly refuses credit for the mere existence of a link, whereas the target scores actionable access, deposition and licensing themselves.
No candidate addresses dataset metadata standards, stewardship plans, intended-use limitations, or ethical/privacy and misuse guidance.

K06 shares the topic of dataset description but scores only whether concrete scale/composition numbers are given, not provenance, collection timeframe, filtering rules, or representativeness of the final sample.
No candidate scores accessibility of materials, inclusive language, or multilingual provision.

Hype-calibration candidates (K40, K45, K09, K46) cover only the 'without hype' fragment and say nothing about whether background, design, results and conclusions are all present and accurately reflected.

The target bundles evidence-aligned interpretation, contextualization with prior work, limitations and implications, while each nearby candidate covers a single strand (K40/K54 overclaiming; K08/K15/K59 limitations; K32/K42 prior-work engagement), so none is substitutable for the whole.
K16 and K46 score interpretability and precision of reported numbers but not the definition, timing of assessment, or primary/secondary prioritization of outcome measures, which is the target's core.
